sequences.title: Two-Variable Thinking: Rules That Travel in Pairs

screens.title: Variables come in pairs now
lines: You can evaluate 3x + 2 in your sleep, and the coordinate plane is home turf — all four quadrants.
New power: variables now arrive in PAIRS that change together. Minutes pass, rows of knitting grow — one moves, the other answers.

vocab.meaning: the input you choose or that ticks on its own, like minutes passing
the output that responds — its value depends on the input, like rows knitted

screens.framing: No grade, just explore: what would YOU try? Even a wild guess teaches your brain what to listen for.

screens.title: Tables are graphs in disguise
lines: Every row of a table is secretly a point (x, y) — and you already know exactly where points live.
Plot a rule's pairs and they snap into a straight line: y = kx lines launch from (0, 0), while y = x + a lines start a steps higher.

items.prompt: Amal posts a cat video. It collects 3 new views every minute, steady as a metronome. How many views after 7 minutes — and can you feel the RULE connecting minutes and views?
items.hint: Try tiny cases: 1 minute → 3 views, 2 minutes → 6 views… what's happening each minute?
items.explanation: views = 3 × minutes, so 7 minutes → 21 views. You just uncovered a two-variable rule — the whole skill in one move.

items.prompt: Cookies vs trays: each tray holds 12 cookies. Let's build the rule machine together.

steps.text: Meet the pair: t = trays Amal bakes, c = cookies that exist. She CHOOSES t; c just obeys. So t is independent and c is dependent.

check.question: Which variable responds instead of being chosen?
options: c — the cookie count reacts to the trays
t — the trays react to the cookies
Both are chosen freely

steps.text: Build a table: t: 1, 2, 3 → c: 12, 24, 36. Every row obeys the same secret.
Name the secret: each c is exactly 12 × its t. In symbols: c = 12t — a multiply rule (the y = kx family).

check.question: What does the 12 in c = 12t describe?
options: Cookies per ONE tray
The number of trays
The biggest batch allowed

steps.text: Now the rule predicts ANYTHING: t = 9 → c = 12 × 9 = 108. One small equation outruns an infinite table. 🍪

items.prompt: Your turn to finish one. On Duolingo, every lesson Amal completes awards 10 XP.
items.hint: Feed L = 6 into the rule x = 10L.
items.explanation: x = 10L turns any lesson count into XP: 10 × 6 = 60. Rules answer questions tables haven't even asked yet.

items.prompt: Not every rule multiplies. Lily the cat is exactly 3 years older than Milo — always was, always will be.

lines: Variables: m = Milo's age, l = Lily's age

items.hint: Lily's age is always Milo's age plus the same number.
items.explanation: Add rules (the y = x + a family) keep a constant GAP: the cats age together, forever 3 apart.

items.prompt: Two mystery tables walk into the Signal Spire. Let's find each one's rule — and its graph fingerprint.

check.question: Which check actually proves y = 4x?
options: Every y ÷ x equals 4, in every row
y goes up by 4 each row, so it must be ×4
The first row works, and that's enough

steps.text: Table 2: x: 1, 2, 3, 4 → y: 5, 6, 7, 8. Multiply fails (5 = 5×1 but 6 ≠ 5×2). Test the gap instead: 5−1 = 4, 6−2 = 4, 7−3 = 4 ✓. Rule: y = x + 4.

check.question: Why test EVERY row, not just the first?
options: One row fits many rules — all the rows pin down the real one
The first row is usually a misprint
Rules only work for big numbers

steps.text: Graph time: Table 1's rows are the points (1, 4), (2, 8), (3, 12), (4, 16) — they line up and aim straight through (0, 0).
Table 2's points (1, 5), (2, 6), (3, 7), (4, 8) also make a line, but it crosses the y-axis at (0, 4). Same straight style, different launch pad — that's how you tell the families apart at a glance.

items.prompt: Crack the rule hiding in this table — no story attached, pure signal.
items.hint: Divide each y by its partner x. A constant answer means a multiply rule.
items.explanation: Every y is 5 times its x, so y = 5x. Constant quotient = the y = kx family.

items.prompt: Another mystery table — but this one refuses to multiply. Find its rule.

lines: Test multiply: 8 ÷ 1 = 8, but 11 ÷ 4 is not 8 — not y = kx

items.hint: When multiply fails, check the gap y − x in every row.
items.explanation: The gap holds at 7 in every row, so y = x + 7 — add rules keep a constant difference.

items.prompt: Last one — you drive. A wizard bookshop sells spell-books for 9 galleons each. Write the rule, then put it to work.

lines: Rule for the cost c of b spell-books: c = [[9]]b
Its graph launches from the origin (0, [[0]]) — the mark of a multiply rule

items.hint: 9 galleons EACH is a per-one price — which rule family has a 'per one'?
items.explanation: c = 9b prices any stack of books, and like every y = kx rule its line passes through (0, 0).

items.prompt: Amal scoops kibble into Biscuit's bowl: the more scoops s she pours, the heavier the bowl w gets. Which variable is DEPENDENT?
items.answer: w — the weight responds to the scoops
options: w — the weight responds to the scoops
s — the scoops respond to the weight
Both are independent
Neither — weight and scoops are unrelated
items.hint: Which one reacts, and which one does Amal choose?
items.explanation: Amal chooses the scoops; the weight has no say — it just responds. Responding is what 'dependent' means.

items.prompt: The rule y = 2x makes pairs. Tap its point where x = 2.
items.hint: When x = 2, y = 2 × 2.
items.explanation: x = 2 gives y = 4, landing at (2, 4) — every pair a rule makes is a point on its line.

items.prompt: A table reads x: 1, 2, 3 → y: 5, 10, 15. Which rule fits EVERY row?
options: y = 5x
y = x + 4
y = x + 5
y = 10x
items.hint: Check all three rows, not just the first.
items.explanation: y = x + 4 fits row one only (1 + 4 = 5); y = 5x delivers 5, 10, 15 — every row agrees.

items.prompt: Amal's scarf already has 12 rows before snack break. After it, she adds exactly 1 row per minute — rule: r = m + 12.
items.hint: Each minute count just gains 12.
items.explanation: r = m + 12 turns minutes into rows with one hop: +12 every time.

items.prompt: Amal reads at a steady pace, so pages finished depend on minutes spent reading. Which is the INDEPENDENT variable?
items.answer: Minutes spent reading — Amal decides how long
options: Minutes spent reading — Amal decides how long
Pages finished — the pages control the clock
The number of chapters in the book
Neither — they change separately
items.hint: Independent = the one being chosen, not the one reacting.
items.explanation: Time is what Amal controls; the page count rides along. Independent drives, dependent rides.

items.prompt: Every muffin tin holds the same number of muffins. Complete the relationship table.
items.hint: First find muffins per ONE tin: 18 ÷ 3.
items.explanation: The rule m = 6t hides in the table: 6 muffins per tin gives 42 and 60.

items.prompt: Amal's Swahili word count: she started knowing 5 words and locks in 1 new word each day — w = d + 5. Tap the point for day 4.
items.hint: Day 4 means w = 4 + 5; days go on the x-axis.
items.explanation: (4, 9): the rule turns every day into a point, and the points march in a perfect line.

items.prompt: Support station: turn Amal's knitting table into a rule, then make it predict.

lines: Each r is its m times [[2]]
Rule: r = 2m, so 15 minutes gives r = [[30]]

items.hint: Divide any r by its m to find the multiplier.
items.explanation: r = 2m fits every row, then predicts row 30 at minute 15 — tables end, rules don't.

items.prompt: A graph line starts at (0, 8) and rises 2 units for every 1 week across. Which story matches it?
items.answer: A savings jar starts with $8 and grows by $2 each week
options: A savings jar starts with $8 and grows by $2 each week
A savings jar starts empty and grows by $8 each week
A savings jar starts with $2 and grows by $8 each week
A savings jar starts with $8 and shrinks by $2 each week
items.hint: The y-axis crossing is the starting amount; the climb is the per-week change.
items.explanation: (0, 8) means $8 before any weeks pass, and rising 2 per week means +$2 weekly — the rule y = 2x + 8.

items.prompt: Sort each rule into its family: multiply rules SCALE x, add rules give x a head start.
items.hint: Ask of each rule: is x being scaled, or shifted?
items.explanation: kx rules scale x (even by 0.5); x + a rules shift it. The size of the number doesn't matter — the operation does.

items.prompt: Match each table to the rule that fits EVERY row.
items.hint: Test multiply first (is y ÷ x constant?), then the gap (is y − x constant?).
items.explanation: Constant quotient → multiply rule; constant gap → add rule. Every row must agree before a rule wins.

items.prompt: A goblin read a table and announced a rule. Tap the step where its logic broke.

segments: Step A: the first row shows x = 1 and y = 6
Step B: 6 × 1 = 6 ✓, so the rule is y = 6x
Step C: prediction — when x = 5, y will be 30

items.hint: A rule has to survive EVERY row of the table.
items.explanation: Row two breaks it: 6 × 2 = 12, not 7. Testing all rows reveals the real rule, y = x + 5.

items.prompt: Read points straight off the rule y = x + 4 — its graph is a perfectly straight line.

lines: At x = 3 the line passes through the point (3, [[7]])
It crosses the y-axis, where x = 0, at (0, [[4]])

items.hint: Plug each x into the rule; the y-axis means x = 0.
items.explanation: (3, 7) and (0, 4) both obey y = x + 4 — add rules cross the y-axis at their head-start number.

items.prompt: Legendary: two savings plans. Plan A: y = 5x (save $5 a week from zero). Plan B: y = 3x + 8 (an $8 head start, then $3 a week). After how many weeks do the plans hold equal money?
items.hint: Equal money means 5x = 3x + 8 — an equation with x on both sides, your specialty.
items.explanation: 5x = 3x + 8 gives 2x = 8, so x = 4 — both plans hold $20 in week 4.

items.prompt: Legendary: Amal owns 14 K-pop photocards and adds 3 per week (y = 3x + 14). Zuri owns 2 and adds 5 per week (y = 5x + 2). When the collections become equal, how many photocards does EACH collector own?
items.hint: First find the week: 3x + 14 = 5x + 2. Then feed that week back into either rule.
items.explanation: 3x + 14 = 5x + 2 gives x = 6, and 3(6) + 14 = 5(6) + 2 = 32 cards each.

items.prompt: Legendary: the Graph Gryphon guards the single point where the lines y = 4x and y = x + 9 cross. Which point is it?
items.hint: At the crossing point, 4x and x + 9 are the SAME number.
items.explanation: 4x = x + 9 gives 3x = 9, so x = 3 and y = 12 — only (3, 12) satisfies both rules at once.
